answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through a bounded-length random walk, so influence is governed by transition probability rather than raw identity count. A Sybil grove may whisper mutual endorsements, but if its external cut is sparse, its conductance φ is low; min-cut transitivity and mixing bounds limit probability mass crossing into the honest haven, giving aggregate voting weight at most proportional to Lφ under stationary or controlled starts, rather than the cluster’s size.
